title: M3 StackVM red-team adversarial test report
principle: Each case drives malicious or malformed contract bytecode through the REAL StackVM.Execute path (vm) and/or the full ApplyTx -> applyContractTx -> StackVM + AddBlock StateRoot re-derivation pipeline (chain) — the same entrypoints block validation uses. Every case asserts the four M3 VM safety invariants under attack: (1) no crash/panic, (2) gas-bounded termination (GasUsed==GasLimit on OOG, never a hang), (3) no state corruption (reverting/OOG frames commit nothing; no cross-contract storage leak or clobber), (4) determinism (identical input+state -> identical StateRoot across independent runs and across mining vs validation derivation). No production vm/chain/state code was modified and no validation was weakened; tests only ADD coverage and reuse in-package helpers.

adversarial_cases.scenario: Bytecode SSTORE slot0=7 then JUMPDEST; PUSH1 5; JUMP -> jumps back forever (unbounded loop). GasLimit 1,000,000.
adversarial_cases.expected: Terminates via ErrOutOfGas (not a hang); GasUsed == GasLimit; the whole message reverts so the pre-loop SSTORE (slot0=7) is wiped back to zero.

adversarial_cases.scenario: Underflow: ADD/SUB/MUL/SSTORE/JUMP and PUSH1;SSTORE on an empty/short stack. Overflow: 1025 straight-line PUSH1 ops (> MaxStack 1024).
adversarial_cases.expected: Underflow variants revert with ErrStackUnderflow; overflow reverts with ErrStackOverflow. No panic in any variant.
adversarial_cases.receipt_evidence: 6/6 underflow codes -> Receipt{Success:false, Err:ErrStackUnderflow}; overflow -> Receipt{Success:false, Err:ErrStackOverflow}; no panic.

adversarial_cases.scenario: JUMP to non-JUMPDEST (offset=STOP), JUMP out of bounds (offset 255), JUMP into PUSH2 immediate data (0x5b byte that is NOT a real JUMPDEST), and JUMPI taken to a bad destination.
adversarial_cases.expected: All four revert with ErrInvalidJump; jumping into PUSH-data 0x5b is rejected (validJumpdests excludes immediates); no panic / no out-of-range indexing.

adversarial_cases.scenario: Contract A writes slot0=42 (committed). Contract B (different address) SLOADs slot0 and RETURNs it.
adversarial_cases.expected: B reads its OWN storage (zero), NOT A's 42 -> no cross-contract leakage; A's slot0 stays 42 and B's slot0 stays 0 -> no cross-contract corruption.
adversarial_cases.receipt_evidence: A.slot0==0x2a; B.ReturnData==32 zero bytes (SLOAD saw 0); A.slot0 still 0x2a after B ran; B.slot0==0.

adversarial_cases.scenario: Contract SSTOREs slot0=7 (affordable) then SSTOREs slot1=9 which exhausts gas mid-execution. Run at VM level (GasLimit 6000) and through the chain as a deployed contract call (callGas 6000).
adversarial_cases.expected: VM: whole message reverts -> slot0 and slot1 both unchanged (zero), GasUsed==GasLimit. Chain/node: the already-applied SSTORE is reverted, the sender nonce still advances, and the full gas budget is consumed (no refund on OOG).
adversarial_cases.receipt_evidence: VM: Receipt{Success:false, Err:ErrOutOfGas, GasUsed:6000}; slot0==slot1==0. Chain: slot0==slot1==0; sender nonce 1->2; balance = (10,000,000 - GasCreate) - 6000 (full call gas consumed).

adversarial_cases.scenario: Non-trivial contract exercising arithmetic (5+3) + SSTORE (slot0=8) + inter-contract CALL of a counter. Run the SAME execution twice on fresh states (VM), and mine deploy/deploy/call blocks then replay them via AddBlock on a FRESH same-genesis chain (chain).
adversarial_cases.expected: VM: two independent runs produce identical StateRoot. Chain: mining-side derivation (buildBlock) and validation-side re-derivation (AddBlock on chain B) yield identical StateRoot; any nondeterminism would cause AddBlock to reject with ErrBadStateRoot. Post-state: caller slot0==8, callee slot0==1.
adversarial_cases.receipt_evidence: VM: root1==root2. Chain A/B: all blocks accepted on both chains; cA.StateRoot()==cB.StateRoot(); caller.slot0==8, callee.slot0==1.

adversarial_cases.scenario: Contract A CALLs B; B CALLs back into A -> mutual recursion with no base case (reentrancy). (a) generous gas, (b) tight gas budget, (c) determinism check.
adversarial_cases.expected: (a) With generous gas the recursion terminates at the call-depth limit (deeper CALLs push 0 without executing) and unwinds to Success -> no infinite recursion, no panic. (b) With a tight budget the shared gas meter bounds it -> ErrOutOfGas, GasUsed==GasLimit, no panic. (c) The depth-bounded run yields identical StateRoot across independent runs.
adversarial_cases.receipt_evidence: (a) Receipt{Success:true}; (b) Receipt{Success:false, Err:ErrOutOfGas, GasUsed:100000}; (c) root1==root2; no panic in any sub-case.

adversarial_cases.scenario: (a) PUSH32 with only 1 immediate byte before end-of-code (truncated). (b) CALLDATALOAD at offset 255 with empty calldata. (c) CALLDATALOAD at offset 0 with 4-byte calldata (window straddles the end).
adversarial_cases.expected: (a) Missing immediate bytes zero-padded; execution completes with no out-of-range panic. (b) Returns a 32-byte zero word. (c) Returns the in-range bytes (0xaabbccdd) followed by zero padding. No slice out-of-range panic in any variant.
adversarial_cases.receipt_evidence: (a) Receipt{Success:true}; (b) ReturnData==32 zero bytes; (c) ReturnData==aabbccdd000...0; no panic.

summary.note: No adversarial case revealed a defect. Malicious/malformed bytecode could not crash the node (no panics), could not exceed its gas budget (unbounded loops and reentrancy terminate via ErrOutOfGas with GasUsed==GasLimit or via the call-depth limit), could not read or corrupt another contract's storage (SLOAD isolation + no cross-contract clobber), and produced deterministic results (identical StateRoot across repeated executions and across mining vs validation re-derivation). OOG/reverting frames commit nothing while the sender nonce still advances and gas is consumed at the chain level. Truncated PUSH immediates and out-of-range CALLDATALOAD are zero-padded per spec with no out-of-range indexing.
